items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The message.py block is hard to follow: `try: DNS_NAME.encode('ascii') except AttributeError: domain = DNS_NAME except UnicodeEncodeError: ... else: domain = DNS_NAME` has no comment explaining why AttributeError is caught (DNS_NAME is normally a CachedDnsName object).

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The `.encode('idna').decode('ascii')` call is copied into both utils.py and message.py. The message.py conversion is redundant once get_fqdn already converts, and there is no shared helper like the reference's `punycode()`.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Only specific exceptions are caught (UnicodeEncodeError, AttributeError) and nothing is silently swallowed. ASCII hostnames come through unchanged. There are no magic constants.

items.name: Conversion is encoding-independent and safe for ASCII names
items.name_zh: 转换与编码无关且不影响 ASCII 主机名
items.evidence: The conversion happens at the source (`socket.getfqdn().encode('idna').decode('ascii')`), so it works for every encoding and ASCII hosts are unchanged. But the same idna conversion is repeated inline in message.py instead of done once.
